title: Troubleshooting Automation with Claude
tagline: From ServiceNow acknowledgement to reason, action and next action
audience: Network operations, load balancer and data centre engineers, NOC and service desk teams, IT automation leads in India and worldwide
prerequisites: Basic networking and load balancer concepts (VIP, pool, HA)
Comfort with a CLI such as F5 tmsh or NetScaler shell
Familiarity with ServiceNow incidents is helpful, not required
outcomes: Explain the incident-to-resolution workflow in ServiceNow and where an agent can and cannot act
Set up Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK and MCP servers scoped to incident triage with read-only tools by default
Pull incidents through the ServiceNow Table API, draft the acknowledgement mail and ask for the primary troubleshooting details that are missing
Collect typed evidence from F5, NetScaler, Radware, other load balancers (Anaya LB) and Cisco ACI and have Claude suggest ranked CLI troubleshooting steps as structured JSON
Enforce read-only versus state-changing command classes, human approval and a full audit trail into ServiceNow work notes
Generate and post the reason, action and next action template and ship a tested troubleshooting page
tools: ServiceNow Table API and Flow Designer

modules.title: The troubleshooting workflow and the ServiceNow incident lifecycle
topics: Incident states, assignment groups, acknowledgement mail and the first troubleshooting reply as they happen today
Mapping the manual workflow: ticket lands, details requested, evidence gathered, steps suggested, resolution note written
Where an agent may act (read, draft, explain) and where it may not (change a device, close a ticket) without a person
The lab: a ServiceNow developer instance, lab load balancers and a Cisco ACI sandbox
modules.lab: Walk one real-style incident from creation to resolution by hand and record every decision an engineer makes.
modules.deliverable: Annotated workflow map and automation boundaries.

modules.title: Setting up Claude Code, the Agent SDK and MCP for incident triage
topics: Claude Code project configuration, CLAUDE.md conventions and permission rules for this workflow
Claude Agent SDK: sessions, tool definitions, structured JSON outputs and retries
MCP servers for ServiceNow and for device read-only queries, with tool allowlists
Keeping credentials in environment and vault, never in prompts or transcripts
modules.lab: Build and register a read-only ServiceNow MCP server and a read-only device MCP server and call them from an Agent SDK script.
modules.deliverable: Working agent environment with scoped tools.

modules.title: Incident intake through the Table API and the acknowledgement mail
topics: Querying incident and sys_journal_field through the ServiceNow Table API and validating records with Pydantic
A primary troubleshooting checklist: affected VIP or service, symptom, start time, scope, last change, error text
Claude compares the ticket against the checklist and lists exactly which details are missing
Drafting the acknowledgement mail with the missing-details questions; a person reviews and sends
modules.lab: Ingest five synthetic incidents, generate the missing-details list and acknowledgement draft for each, and post it as a work note.
modules.deliverable: Intake service and acknowledgement mail generator.

modules.title: Evidence collection from load balancers and ACI
topics: F5: tmsh show ltm virtual and pool, iControl REST /mgmt/tm/ltm and /mgmt/tm/sys for stats and logs
Citrix NetScaler NITRO API: lbvserver, servicegroup and HA node status; Radware Alteon and other load balancers (Anaya LB) through their CLI
Cisco APIC REST API: fault, health score and endpoint lookups for the affected tenant
Typed evidence records with device, timestamp, command and raw output; nothing inferred without data
modules.lab: Write deterministic collectors for each platform and run them against the lab devices for one incident.

modules.title: Claude suggests troubleshooting steps as structured JSON
topics: Prompt design: ticket plus evidence in, ranked likely causes out, each with a confirming CLI command and expected result
JSON schema for a suggested step: platform, command, class (read_only or state_changing), rationale, evidence citations
Testing the prompt with missing, stale and contradictory evidence; unknowns must be marked
Comparing suggestions against a vendor-documented playbook for the same symptom
modules.lab: Build the suggestion agent, run it on three incidents and score its first-step accuracy against the engineer's manual notes.

modules.title: Guardrails, approvals and audit for incident automation
topics: Command classification and allowlists: read-only commands may run in the lab, state-changing commands always wait
Approval record: who approved, which command, which device, when, and the output captured
Writing every action to an audit log and to ServiceNow work notes through the Table API
Failure modes: wrong device, wrong incident, hallucinated command; detection and fail-closed behaviour
modules.lab: Add the approval gate and audit writer, then try to push a state-changing command through without approval and watch it refuse.

modules.title: Running approved steps and reading the result
topics: Executing approved commands through SSH and REST wrappers with timeouts and output capture
Claude interprets command output against the expected result and proposes the next step
Loop control: maximum steps, stop conditions and escalation to a senior engineer
ServiceNow Flow Designer trigger that starts the loop when an incident is assigned to the group
modules.lab: Run the suggest, approve, execute, interpret loop end to end on one incident until the cause is confirmed.

modules.title: The reason, action and next action template
topics: Template fields: reason (root cause with evidence), action (what was done, by whom, approved by whom), next action (owner and due date)
Claude drafts the template from the evidence bundle and command outputs with a citation for every claim
Posting resolution notes and close codes to the incident and creating a knowledge article draft
Template variants per symptom family: VIP down, pool member flapping, HA sync failure, certificate expiry
modules.lab: Generate the template for the resolved incident, review it, post it to ServiceNow and create the knowledge article.
modules.deliverable: Reason, action and next action generator.

modules.title: The troubleshooting page: service, tests and delivery
topics: FastAPI troubleshooting page: incident queue, evidence view, suggested steps, approve and reject buttons, audit tab
pytest suites for intake, classification and template generation with recorded device output as fixtures
GitHub pull requests and Actions: lint, tests and a prompt regression check on every change
Operating the page: runbook, on-call handover and what to do when the agent is wrong
modules.lab: Assemble the page, write the regression suite and merge through a reviewed pull request with Actions green.

modules.title: Capstone: incident to resolution note, end to end
topics: A new incident lands in ServiceNow; the team runs the full workflow from acknowledgement to posted template
Acceptance criteria review: no device change without approval, every claim cited, every action logged
Demo and limitations statement

capstone: A repeatable troubleshooting workflow that picks up a ServiceNow incident, asks for the missing primary troubleshooting details, collects evidence from F5, NetScaler, Radware, other load balancers (Anaya LB) and Cisco ACI, suggests ranked CLI steps, runs only approved commands, and posts a reason, action and next action template with a full audit trail.

narration: hook

An incident lands in ServiceNow at nine at night. The acknowledgement mail goes out, and then the questions begin. Which V I P? Since when? What changed? Who is looking at it? And the engineer on call is typing the same first five commands they typed last week.
hook

What if an agent read the ticket, asked for the missing details, pulled the evidence from the load balancer, and suggested the exact C L I commands to run next? Troubleshooting, automated, with a person still in charge of every change.
intro
Gennoor Tech presents Troubleshooting Automation with Claude.
story

One incident in. One resolution note out. You build the troubleshooting workflow in ten modules, and every module ends with something that actually runs. Claude reads, plans and explains. Deterministic Python collects the evidence and updates the ticket. A person approves anything that touches a device. And every step is logged, in your audit trail and in the ServiceNow work notes.
path0

You start with the incident lifecycle in ServiceNow, from the moment the ticket is created to the acknowledgement mail and the first troubleshooting reply. You map where an agent may act and where it may not. Then you set up Claude Code, the Claude Agent S D K and M C P servers for this exact workflow, with a read only ServiceNow tool, a read only device tool, and nothing else. Credentials stay in the vault, never in a prompt.
path0

Then intake. You pull the incident through the ServiceNow Table A P I, validate it, and let Claude compare it against a primary troubleshooting checklist. Affected V I P, symptom, start time, scope, last change. The agent lists what is missing and drafts the clarification mail. An engineer reviews it and sends it.
path1

Day two is evidence and diagnosis. Deterministic collectors run F5 t m s h and iControl REST, the NetScaler NITRO A P I, Radware Alteon and other load balancers, and the Cisco A P I C REST interface, and return typed facts with a device, a timestamp and the raw output. Claude turns those facts into a ranked list of likely causes, and for each cause the exact C L I command that confirms or rules it out. Structured J S O N, with a citation for every claim, never free text.
path2

Then the guardrails. Every suggested command is classified read only or state changing. Read only commands can run in the lab automatically. Anything else waits for an engineer to approve, and the approval, the command and the output are written to the audit log and to the ServiceNow work notes. You will try to push a change through without approval, and you will watch it refuse. Then you run the full loop. Suggest, approve, execute, interpret, until the cause is confirmed or a senior engineer is paged.
path3

Day three is the template. Reason, action, next action. Claude drafts it from the evidence it was given, cites the command output behind every line, and marks what it could not verify. You post it to the incident through the Table A P I, with the close code, and you create the knowledge article the next incident will reuse.
path3

You finish by wiring it all into a troubleshooting page. A FastAPI service with the incident queue, the evidence, the suggested steps, the approve and reject buttons and the audit tab. Tested with pytest against recorded device output, and shipped through a reviewed GitHub pull request with Actions green.
labs

Every lab runs against a ServiceNow developer instance, lab load balancers and a Cisco A C I sandbox, with synthetic incidents that have real symptoms. You will watch the agent ask the right question, run the right command, and refuse the wrong one. And in the capstone a fresh incident lands and your team takes it from acknowledgement to posted resolution note.
stats
Ten modules that run. Three days, hands on. Four device platforms. And zero device changes without a person saying yes.
who

This course is for network operations, load balancer and data centre engineers, N O C and service desk teams, and I T automation leads in India and worldwide. You need basic networking, comfort with a C L I, and some Python. Familiarity with ServiceNow incidents helps, but it is not required.
cta
